reelection.rule: Rule: next even-year November for this House term. legislators-current.yaml ends the current term on 2027-01-03. The even-year November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file has no election day, so no day of the month is shown.

vote_frequency.label: In this cached set only (the latest 40 House roll calls, not a lifetime record): 40 of 40. Yea or Aye: 13. Nay or No: 13. Not Voting: 14. Of 26 Yea or Nay votes where the Democratic majority could be computed, 26 (100%) matched that majority (majority = the side most of that party's members voting Yea or Nay took; on average 207 members of that party voted Yea or Nay per roll call).

stands_for.majority_rule: Party majority = the Yea/Nay side taken by most members of that party who voted Yea or Nay on that roll call, counted from the party code in the roll-call XML (all members, including ones no longer serving). Ties have no majority.

said_voted.caption: Posts are shown as written. A post is matched to a vote only when it names the bill number or the bill's official title. A post can mention a bill for many reasons.
said_voted.topic_caption: Recent posts grouped by simple keyword rules that are identical for every member (published at /x_topic_rules.json). A post listed under a topic is not claimed to be about any specific vote; a post can appear under more than one topic.

posts.text:
Our veterans fought for us. Now, we must fight for them.

I proudly presented the $3 million federal earmark I secured for CRC Leadership, Inc., and broke ground on the Sergeant La David Johnson Veterans Villas, a new housing development that will provide safe homes for veterans in our community.

Named in honor of our hometown hero, these villas will honor his sacrifice by serving those who served our nation.

We made headlines for a promise worth keeping: a safe place for our veterans to call home. The Sergeant La David Johnson Veterans Villas will bring new housing for veterans to our community. 

Watch the coverage of this meaningful step forward. https://t.co/iCzqzNmBRn

This Miami girl’s heart is full! To see the North Dade Regional Library become the Frederica S. Wilson Regional Library is an honor I will treasure forever.

Thank you to everyone who made this moment possible. 

My name may stand above the doors, but my hope is that every child who walks through them will stand taller because of what they discover inside.

A library is a gateway to knowledge, opportunity, and brighter futures. I am deeply honored to have the North Dade Regional Library named in my honor. 

This recognition reflects a lifelong commitment to education and empowering generations to come. I look forward to celebrating https://t.co/QbusqrzDpQ

Our veterans fought for us, and we must fight for them. I am proud to have secured the $3 million earmark to build these much-needed homes for veterans, named for our hometown hero, Sgt. La David Johnson, who gave his life in Niger and was posthumously awarded the Silver Star for valor.

Join me November 9 at 11 a.m. as we break ground and honor his legacy.

Florida’s future is shaped by those who show up and make their voices heard. Our communities and future generations are counting on us. Your voice is your power. 

Get out and vote! https://t.co/fAbFG3PT5N

Our entrepreneurs deserve the resources to build, own, and prosper. I was proud to present $850,000 that I secured for the Liberty Square Launchpad Small Business Incubator, in partnership with the City of Miami and the Miami-Dade Chamber of Commerce.

This investment will help small businesses grow and our community prosper.

Opa-locka, you have always had a place in my heart. I am deeply honored to receive the Key to the City from Mayor John H. Taylor, Jr. Thank you, Mayor, for your service and this meaningful recognition. 

Fighting for our children and families has been the privilege of my life, https://t.co/0sviJ2G2Uv

As the first and only Bahamian descendant to serve in Congress, I am deeply honored to receive the Order of Excellence, the highest award a noncitizen can receive from the Bahamian government.

Thank you to Governor-General Dame Cynthia A. Pratt, the National Honours Committee, https://t.co/IkLxHWCajc

Tomorrow, the Police & Youth Conference comes to Hard Rock Stadium! In partnership with the Miami Dolphins and the 5000 Role Models of Excellence Project, we’re bringing young men and law enforcement together to build trust, strengthen relationships, and create a stronger https://t.co/u2Tccc1mfZ
@politico This is wonderful 🩷

North Miami Beach Mayor Michael Joseph attended the 5000 Role Models of Excellence Project’s club meeting at North Miami Beach Senior High School. Mayor Joseph is a proud graduate of the school’s 5000 Role Models program. https://t.co/o5V474F9ZA

Our children deserve every opportunity to succeed. I’m proud to join the Department of Justice in presenting over $1 million to the 5000 Role Models of Excellence Project.

As its founder, I know this investment means more mentorship, more opportunities, and brighter futures for boys across South Florida. Thank you to the leaders across Miami-Dade whose partnership and commitment help our boys thrive.
Happy Birthday to our Vice President Kamala Harris! Wishing you a year filled with love, joy, and abundant blessings! https://t.co/Rh74sEvBky

People will walk through The Obama Presidential Center and, when their visit is over, they will leave. I won’t. I am featured in the voting rights exhibit because I have spent my life fighting for a simple truth: our votes are our power, and no one has the right to take that power away.

My story will remain there. So will the charge to protect the vote.

When we invest in our students, we invest in the future of our entire community. I’m proud to have secured $850,000 for Miami Dade College to strengthen its programs and open more doors for students.

Thank you, President Madeline Pumariega and Dr. Malou C. Harrison, Executive Vice President and Provost, for your leadership, and to the community leaders who joined us in supporting our students’ success!
@ABurgessEdu @5000RoleBCPS I love love this 🩷

I founded the 5000 Role Models because our boys deserve a future worth fighting for. At our North Region Tie-Tying Ceremony, I proudly presented a check to invest in that future.

Prevention, not detention. WE ARE 5000! https://t.co/MAg0cS9PPZ

The world is watching Florida. The decisions made at the ballot box will shape the future of this state for generations to come. This election is too important to sit on the sidelines.

Every voice matters. Every vote counts. https://t.co/dzc7fOFI0Q

As a former elementary school principal, my heart breaks for the families in Bend, Oregon. Every parent deserves to see their child come home from school. I’m praying for this community and everyone affected by this tragedy. 

Our children deserve to be safe. https://t.co/0CiWKmGg3t

Florida, the stakes are too high to stay home. The leaders elected today will make decisions families live with for years. 

Show up and VOTE! https://t.co/0RjM7Jjrtj

Don Lemon traveled to Miami Gardens, and it was wonderful to welcome him to Pumps, Pearls and Politics®! We had a powerful conversation about Florida’s future. Now, let’s take that energy to the ballot box! https://t.co/WnDXX9wrqS

Nolan Xavier Wells’ family deserves answers. I have called on the National Park Service to conduct a prompt, exhaustive investigation into his death on Horn Island, pursue every lead, and keep his family informed.

Nolan’s life mattered. His family’s search for the truth deserves the full weight of the federal government.
@PollTracker2024 Thank you Bernie
@RepTroyCarter I love love love this !

Nolan Xavier Wells was a son whose life was precious and whose future was full of promise. His family deserves answers.

I’ve called on the National Park Service to conduct a thorough investigation into his death, pursue every lead, and keep his family informed. We owe Nolan and his loved ones the truth.

Now that I have your attention, make sure you have a plan to vote! 🗳️ Your voice matters, your vote matters, and every election is an opportunity to make your voice heard.

VOTE! VOTE! VOTE! https://t.co/9P85KMHLkI

Miami-Dade, this is your opportunity to be heard. Join Superintendent Rafael A. Villalobos for a series of town hall meetings across District 24 to share your voice, ask questions, and help shape the future of our public schools. https://t.co/DbD8I17ID5

I’m proud to announce $8,824,314 in grants for four of Florida’s HBCUs: Florida Memorial University, Florida A&M University, Bethune-Cookman College, and Edward Waters College.

Our HBCUs have opened doors for generations of students and shaped leaders who changed this nation. They deserve the resources to keep opening those doors. I will always fight for their future.

Glaucoma can steal sight before symptoms appear. That’s why I introduced the Glaucoma Vision Act: to expand screenings, bring care to underserved communities, and invest in research. 

Early detection can protect a lifetime of vision. https://t.co/F2UEcbTJod
It takes many hands and many hearts to make moments like these special. Thank you to everyone who showed up with purpose. https://t.co/E4qW5EsKFP

Last week’s CBCF Annual Legislative Conference is one I will carry with me forever. To every family who shared their story, every advocate who stood with us, and every person who worked behind the scenes to bring us together: thank you. You made it possible, and you reminded us why this work must continue.

To my 5000 Role Models, thank you for bringing your energy, your leadership, and your bright futures to last week’s CBCF Annual Legislative Conference. Seeing you stand together in Washington reminded me why I began this work. 

I am so proud of you, and I will always fight for every opportunity you deserve.

Nolan Wells’ name deserves to be remembered, and so does the courage of his parents, Christine Wells-Wonsley and Elmore Wonsley. I was honored to present them with a tribute entered into the Congressional Record, preserving their names and Nolan’s legacy in our nation’s history. https://t.co/JzMEWnsIzY

Standing with Christine Wells-Wonsley and Elmore Wonsley Sr., I thanked them for the courage it takes to carry Nolan Wells’ name, memory and legacy forward. 

Their strength reminds us why this work must continue, and why we can never stop fighting for the lives and futures of our children.

I honored Trayvon Martin, Jordan Davis, Nolan Wells, and King Carter by placing their names and their stories into the Congressional Record. I stood with their parents as we recognized the lives of their sons and the pain no parent should ever have to endure.

Their names must mean more than remembrance. They must move us to action, strengthen our commitment to protecting Black boys, and demand a future where no parent has to stand where they stand today.

At the Day of Healing Prayer Breakfast, the 5000 Role Models handed out roses with a tenderness that spoke louder than words.

I am proud of the care they showed each person they greeted. Their compassion is a form of leadership, and they showed it beautifully. https://t.co/EqZ3asntZl

I want a world where a Black boy’s smile is an ordinary sight, where he can walk into a classroom, down his street and toward his future without fear.

At our CBCF Annual Legislative Conference gathering, I saw that joy in the faces of the 5000 Role Models. It is precious, and it is ours to protect.

I was proud to bring together courageous families and committed advocates for a conversation rooted in truth and focused on solutions. The Role Models led us in prayer, reminding us who this work is for and what is at stake.

The measure of this moment will be found in the laws we change, the resources we deliver and the lives we protect.

We spoke the names of Trayvon Martin, Jordan Davis, Nolan Wells and King Carter as a charge to act. I was honored to present their parents with tributes entered into the Congressional Record, forever preserving their sons’ legacies in our nation’s history.

Our Black boys should not have to become martyrs before America recognizes their humanity. Through this Commission, we will turn remembrance into action and ensure their legacies are never forgotten.

Black men and boys are not problems to be solved. They are scholars, creators, fathers, leaders and the promise of generations still to come.

This Commission exists to ensure that their futures are not determined by neglected schools, unequal systems or the limits others place upon them. We are building a nation that sees their greatness early, invests in it fully and protects it fiercely.

conflicts.caption: These are overlaps in public records, not evidence of a deal. Lobbying can be for or against a bill, and donors' employers didn't necessarily give money.
conflicts.method: Each itemized donor dollar is counted once, under the industry of the donor's self-reported employer; an industry counts if at least one LD-2 client in it lobbied on any bill this member sponsored or voted on.
